summary: A neder against all benefit from someone is stricter than a neder only against his food. The difference is walking on his property and borrowing things that are not used for food.

summary: Someone may help a person who may not benefit from him by paying what that person owes, or returning his lost thing, because that is not counted as a benefit.

chunks.en: Someone forbidden by neder to get any benefit from his friend,
chunks.st: With regard to one prohibited by vow from deriving benefit from another,

chunks.en: the friend may give his half-shekel for him,
chunks.st: if that other person chooses, he may contribute the half-shekel to the Temple on his behalf,

words.note: The half-shekel each Jew gave to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and pay back his debt,
chunks.st: and repay his debt,

chunks.en: and give him back his lost item.
chunks.st: and return his lost item to him,

chunks.en: In a place where people get paid for returning a lost item,
chunks.st: and the one prohibited from benefiting is not considered to have benefited from him. In a place where one takes payment

chunks.en: the benefit should be given to hekdesh.
chunks.st: for returning a lost item, that benefit should fall into the category of consecrated Temple property.

words.note: Hekdesh: money for the Beis HaMikdash.

summary: The mishnah lists more things a person may do for someone who may not benefit from him, like bringing his korbanos or teaching him Torah. It ends with an argument about feeding his animals.
stIntro: The mishna proceeds to list other tasks that one may perform for someone who is prohibited by vow from benefiting from him.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to them:

summary: When someone may not benefit from his friend, the mishnah teaches what they may still do together: visiting, healing, bathing, sleeping, eating, and working.

chunks.en: Someone forbidden by neder to get benefit from his friend, and he comes to visit him when he is sick,
chunks.st: In the case of one for whom benefit from another is forbidden by vow and he enters his house to visit him,

chunks.en: stands, but does not sit.
chunks.st: he stands there but does not sit.

chunks.en: And the friend may heal his body,
chunks.st: And that other person heals him with a cure of the nefesh
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains: healing him, not healing his animals.

chunks.en: but not heal his animals.
chunks.st: but not a cure of mamon.

chunks.en: And he may bathe with him in a big bathtub,
chunks.st: And with regard to another person who is prohibited from deriving benefit from him, one may bathe with him in a large bath [ambati],

chunks.en: but not in a small one.
chunks.st: in which his presence does not affect the other person. However,
chunks.stMore: he may not bathe with him in a small bath, as his presence moderates the temperature of water if it is too hot or too cold, thereby benefiting the other person.

chunks.en: And he may sleep with him in one bed.
chunks.st: And he may sleep with him in one bed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: in the summer,
chunks.st: That is permitted during the days of summer,

chunks.en: but not in the rainy season,
chunks.st: but he may not sleep with him in one bed during the rainy season,

chunks.en: because he helps him.
chunks.explain: He warms the bed for him.
chunks.st: i.e., the winter, because he benefits him

chunks.en: And he may lean with him on a couch,
chunks.st: by warming the bed. And he may recline with him on a divan

chunks.en: and eat with him at the table,
chunks.st: even during the rainy season, as no benefit is involved. And he may eat with him at the same table,

chunks.en: but not from one serving dish,
chunks.st: but not from a common platter

chunks.en: but he may eat with him
chunks.st: from which several people eat, as if one leaves food on the platter, the other derives benefit from him. However, he may eat with him

chunks.en: from a serving dish that goes back.
chunks.explain: A dish that goes back to the host with food left in it.
chunks.st: from a platter that returns
chunks.stMore: to the host, as everyone takes a small portion and leaves food on the platter. No benefit is derived. Since there is enough food for everyone, none of the diners receives part of another’s portion.

chunks.en: He may not eat with him from
chunks.st: One may neither eat with him from

chunks.en: the big bowl in front of workers,
chunks.st: the large vessel of food placed before the laborers,

chunks.en: and he may not work with him in one row,
chunks.st: nor may he work with him in the same row in a vineyard;

chunks.en: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he may work far from him.
chunks.st: He may work in the same row with him provided that he is at a distance from him. If he is close, the other would derive forbidden benefit from him.

summary: In Shemitah year, fruit belongs to everyone. So a person who may not benefit from his friend may then eat fruit hanging out of his friend's field.

chunks.en: Someone forbidden by neder to get benefit from his friend before Shemitah
chunks.st: In the case of one for whom benefit from another is forbidden, before, i.e., a year other than the Sabbatical Year,

words.note: The seventh year, when fields rest and fruit belongs to all.

chunks.en: may not go into his field,
chunks.st: he may neither enter the field

chunks.en: and may not eat from the fruit hanging over.
chunks.st: of that other person, nor eat from

chunks.en: And in Shemitah, he may not go into his field,
chunks.st: the produce that leans out of the field, even if he does not enter the field. And during the Sabbatical Year, when the produce of the trees is ownerless, he may not enter his field;

chunks.en: but he may eat from the fruit hanging over.
chunks.st: however, he may eat from the growths that lean out of the field,

chunks.en: If he made a neder not to get food from him before Shemitah,
chunks.st: as the produce does not belong to the other person. If one vowed before the Sabbatical Year that benefit from another’s food is forbidden for him,

chunks.en: he may go into his field,
chunks.st: he may enter his field;

chunks.en: but may not eat from the fruit.
chunks.st: however, he may not eat of the produce.

chunks.en: And in Shemitah, he may go in and eat.
chunks.st: And during the Sabbatical Year, he may enter the field and may eat the produce.

summary: Someone who may not benefit from his friend may not lend, borrow, buy, or sell with him. The mishnah also tells about a man who made an angry neder about plowing with a cow.

chunks.en: Someone forbidden by neder to get benefit from his friend,
chunks.st: In the case of one for whom benefit from another is forbidden by vow,

chunks.en: the friend may not lend him anything and may not borrow from him,
chunks.st: that other person may neither lend an item to him nor borrow an item from him.

chunks.en: may not lend him money and may not borrow money from him,
chunks.st: Similarly, he may neither lend money to him nor borrow money from him.

chunks.he: וְלֹא יִמְכֹּר לוֹ וְלֹא יִקַּח מִמֶּנּוּ.
chunks.en: and may not sell to him and may not buy from him.
chunks.st: And he may neither sell an item to him nor purchase an item from him.

chunks.st: Lend me your cow.

chunks.en: If he usually plowed by himself,
chunks.st: If it was his typical manner to plow

chunks.en: he is forbidden, and all other people are permitted.
chunks.st: the field himself, then it is prohibited for him to plow his field with that cow but it is permitted for every other person.

chunks.st: If it is not his typical manner to plow

chunks.en: he and all people are forbidden.
chunks.st: the field himself, and he has others plow for him, it is prohibited for him and for every other person to plow his field with that cow, because his intent was to render benefit from plowing with this cow forbidden.
